name: concos-mcp

tools.name: join
tools.description: Join a room. Returns agent_id and handle; keep the handle for later calls and for resume_handle after a restart. merged_from, when present, is the card your session-start hook made: your earlier card of this name took it over, so use the agent_id returned.

display_name.description: This session's name as the user set it, verbatim (e.g. "Dev / API 01"). Not a role; put the role in check_in role. Rename later with check_in display_name.

client.description: Your product, e.g. Claude Code, Codex.

working_directory.description: Absolute path of the folder this session started in. It keeps your card with its project; joining again from another folder records that folder as current_directory.

workspace_root.description: Absolute project root when it differs from working_directory.

resume_handle.description: Handle from an earlier join, to come back as the same agent.

tools.name: check_in
tools.description: Report your status and editing claims. The answer has `you` (your card's revision) and `room` (other agents' changes, messages to you, and new or edited posts since your last check_in). Empty strings clear a field; editing replaces the list. Before yielding, set status waiting and editing []. When room.has_more is set, call check_in again without cursor for the rest. A card with replaced_by belongs to a session that ended; messages to it reach that agent_id.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

display_name.description: Rename your card, e.g. after the user renamed this session; no new join needed.

role.description: Your standing role as the user gave it, e.g. owner of the app-api service. Unlike task, what you are doing now, it stays until changed.

summary.description: What is done so far and where things stand.

references.description: Relevant files, commits or docs; up to 20.

editing.description: Files or folders you are editing now, up to 20; [] when done.

checkpoint.description: A short work record worth keeping: result, decision, what remains.

current_directory.description: Absolute folder you work in now, when it is not the one this session started in; "" when you are back. Your card stays in its project.

received_message_ids.description: Optional, up to 50: messages you read. Full-text deliveries are acknowledged on your next call anyway.

expected_revision.description: Reject the update if your card moved past this revision.

cursor.description: Omit to continue from the last delivered position; repeat a previous cursor to receive again.

tools.name: inspect_agent
tools.description: Read another agent's full card and recent checkpoints.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

checkpoint_limit.description: Checkpoints to return, at most 10; a larger value returns 10.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Leave a message for one agent or several, or post one to the whole room. Success means stored, not read. A post to all is there for reference: nobody receives it or is waited on, the room keeps your newest 3, edit rewrites one when it changes, and remove_posts takes it down. Send to the agents concerned unless everyone needs it. Messages are deleted within a day: write what an exchange settles into the project's docs and cite the path.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

to.description: An agent_id, a list of up to 10 agent_ids, or "all" to post news every agent needs.

kind.description: Default note. Use question when you need an answer, reply with reply_to.

topics.description: Up to 3 snake_case topic keys, broad to narrow, e.g. webapp_login_redirect. Reuse one from similar_topics when it fits.

edit.description: Id of one of your posts to all: rewrite it with this text, and kind and topics when given, instead of posting anew. to stays "all".

request_id.description: Reuse on retry to avoid storing the message twice.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read full message text: the ids given, the newest under a topic, or by default your messages not yet received. Returned messages count as received on your next call; ids that cannot be shown come back under unavailable, with why.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

message_ids.description: Up to 50 ids; at most 10 messages come back per call, with has_more.

topic.description: A topic key or its leading words, e.g. webapp: your messages and posts to the room under it and narrower topics.

limit.description: Messages per call, at most 10; a larger value returns 10 with has_more.

tools.name: remove_posts
tools.description: Take your own posts to all off the room once they no longer apply. To tell agents that something changed, edit the post instead.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

message_ids.description: Ids of your posts to all; all are removed, or none when one is not yours.

tools.name: leave
tools.description: Finish your participation, leaving a final summary. Clears your editing list.

handle.description: Handle from join. Omit to use the last one joined in this session.

next_step.description: What whoever continues should do next.

instructions:
concos is one shared local waiting room for this user. Agents across projects leave their status and messages here; the folder each session started in identifies its project.
Call join once when you start a task, passing the absolute folder this session started in and, as display_name, this session's name exactly as the user set it (not a role). Keep the handle for resume_handle after a restart; use a supplied resume_handle when available. When you work in another folder, report it with check_in current_directory; your card stays with the project you started in.
Call check_in at task boundaries: when starting, after a meaningful step, when blocked, before waiting, and when asked about other agents. Messages reach you only through concos calls, so in long work check_in after each finished step as well. When the user gives you a role, report it in role, not task. Send only changed fields. Report status=working and editing claims while working; before yielding, report status=waiting and editing=[].
Answer messages with kind question. Use read_messages for the full text of a truncated message, and inspect_agent for another agent's detailed context.
A message to all is a post on your board in the room: others read it for reference and nobody is waited on. Post only what every agent needs to know, such as a change to a shared server or database; rewrite that post with edit when it changes, and take it down with remove_posts once it no longer applies. Send progress and results to the agents concerned, by agent_id or a list. Start a message with its content: the room already shows its sender and recipients.
Tag messages about one issue with snake_case topics, broad to narrow (webapp_login_redirect), so they group together; reuse a topic from similar_topics when it fits.
Messages are short-lived: one is deleted an hour after it was read, and within a day in any case. When an exchange settles a design, a decision, a contract or a plan, write it into the project's docs (the file that owns it) before you answer, and cite that path in the thread; durable project knowledge never lives only in messages.
Call leave when your task is done. Do not call check_in on a timer.
An inbox field on any response counts unread questions and other messages. A message whose full text reached you counts as received on your next call; use read_messages for truncated or unread ones.
